Testing macro ideas

How much of a policy move was already priced? When did the central bank act, and what happened afterwards? Compare survey responses, market prices and official records on the same timeline.

Do large auction awards stay on dealers’ books?Follow weekly positions around 164 nominal ten-year Treasury auctions and compare the evidence for individual issues. What moved 2s10s before the Fed spoke?

A flatter curve before a Fed speech could reflect a change in expected short rates, the compensation investors require to hold longer bonds, or both. Compare the observed Treasury move with the two components of the New York Fed’s Adrian–Crump–Moench (ACM) model.

Data, method and interpretation

The observed rates are US Treasury par yields. ACM fits zero-coupon yields. Its two additive components reconstruct the fitted yield, so a gap can remain between the observed and fitted moves. For 2s10s, subtract each two-year change from its corresponding ten-year change. For a single tenor, read the changes in that yield directly.

Use the last jointly observed two- and ten-year Treasury closes strictly before the event. The five-quote option spans four close-to-close intervals. Both endpoints must have ACM estimates. Same-day speeches count once. The non-overlapping option works forward in time within the chosen sample, keeping the next window whose first quote follows the last retained endpoint.

Correlations are Pearson correlations across the displayed dates. Direction counts exclude zero moves in either series. The ACM expected-rate component averages short rates over the selected bond’s life. Estimating the odds of the next FOMC decision requires a meeting-linked instrument or an explicitly identified survey. ACM fits Treasury yields, so the model and the observed slope share underlying market information. A high correlation can partly reflect that construction. The workbook contains revised model estimates, and overlapping windows share observations. The comparisons describe historical co-movement and leave the causal shock unidentified.

Historical comparisons

What survived the tests?

Debt rollovers and currency losses

Does short-term external debt help identify which currencies will fall furthest in a global shock? The relationship varies by episode. In 2008, the six economies with the highest debt-to-reserves ratios had a median three-month currency decline of 8.1%. In 2020 the rank correlation across the 19 matched economies was close to zero.

Dealer inventory and secondary-market demand

On 79 of 109 reopenings, dealers held a higher net position in the same ten-year note at the first report on or after settlement than at the preceding report. Two weeks later, the high-award group had a smaller median increase than the middle group. Dealers can sell in the when-issued market before an auction, distribute the bonds quickly and still finance a customer’s purchase afterwards.
